message.content:
In Ancient Greek, the concept of a **lawgiver** (the person who establishes laws and orders) is expressed by the noun **νόμογένεσθαι** (nomogénesthai).  
- **νόμος** (nomos) – “law”  
- **νόμογένεσθαι** – literally “to make law”; used as a noun to refer to the act or person of lawmaking.

So, when you want to say “who establishes laws and orders” in Ancient Greek, you would refer to the **νόμογένεσθαι** (lawgiver).
